exp3.description: Train tweet-trained models on all tweets, predict binary left/right AllSides article test set (media-based split, left=D, right=R).

tweet_training_data.note: Tweets are 64.1% D; models may be biased toward predicting D on unlabelled text.

article_test_set.note: Center articles excluded; left=D (402, 40.2%), right=R (599, 59.8%). Majority baseline is always-R (59.8%). Tweet-trained models predict D only 26-49% of the time, so they lean R on articles despite 64.1% D training tweets.

paper_results.note: 100 poll-labelled articles from the paper; wide CIs show how noisy that test set is.

error_analysis.note: Top 5 misclassified articles; driving words are those in the article with the highest log-ratio toward the wrong predicted class.

ext1.description: Extension 1: TF-IDF word unigrams + bigrams (no_punct) with logistic regression
ext1.verdict: Held-out members: TF-IDF + bigrams + LR reaches macro F1 0.824 (accuracy 0.833), better than the best earlier model LinearSVC (C=0.06) (0.795, +2.9 points). Articles: macro F1 0.591 (accuracy 0.592), about the same as the paper's count LinearSVC on the same articles (0.587, +0.5 points). Its article accuracy is not above always predicting R (0.598, the article test majority).

ext2.description: Extension 2: Sentence-chunk voting for news articles. Each article is split into tweet-sized chunks, scored with tweet-trained models, and probabilities averaged. Chunk size tuned on validation split only, then evaluated on test split.

ext3.description: Extension 3: In-domain training on AllSides news articles (media-based split). Evaluates binary (left vs right) and 3-class (left vs center vs right) accuracy to quantify the cost of the tweet-to-article domain gap.

model_zoo.dataset: congresstweets with House member party labels
